newsitem.title: UK: UK Oftel appoints 5 new members to fair trade body.
newsitem.headline: UK Oftel appoints 5 new members to fair trade body.

text.p: The Office of Telecommunications (Oftel), the regulatory body for UK's telecom sector, said on Tuesday it had appointed five new members to its Fair Trading Advisory Body.
The new body, formed last December to advise Oftel on enforcement of fair trading conditions, will now have six members including its chairman Jeremy Lever.
The body's job would be to advise Oftel's director general on enforcing the conditions.

The five new members are Mark Armstrong, professor of economic policy at Southampton University, Martin Howe, former director of the competition policy division at office of fair trading, Hans Liesner, former deputy chairman of MMC, Teresa Smallbone, consultant to National Consumer Council and Geoffrey Whittington, professor of financial accounting at Cambridge University.
"They will be a real asset to the advisory body and its work in advancing competition in the UK telecoms market," Don Cruickshank, Oftel's director-general said.
